newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore 1997 growth forecast still 5-7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Singapore 1997 growth forecast still 5-7 percent.

text.p: Singapore's official growth forecast for 1997 remains at five to seven percent, a statement from Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong's office said on Wednesday.

In a letter to Singapore newspapers made available to foreign media, Lee's principal private secretary said the deputy prime minister had not intended to revise the forecast in a speech delivered on Tuesday. Lee said in the speech that Singapore's economy was expected to make steady six to seven percent growth this year and for the next few years.

"DPM Lee wishes to clarify that he made an error. He was speaking generally about the performance of the economy this year and for the next few years, and did not intend to revise (the Ministry of Trade and Industry's) growth forecast of 5-7 percent for 1997," the letter said.
Singapore's full year growth for 1996 was seven percent, significantly below the 8.8 percent expansion of 1995 and the double-digit growth of the previous two years.
Private economists' forecasts for growth this year have generally been around seven percent.
A forecast released on Wednesday by the UN's Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific said Singapore annual growth would average 6.7 percent over the period from 1996 through 2000.
